title: Engineering Assessment of Gerusernay Embankment Dam: Hydrological, Geotechnical, and Construction Performance Analysis
content: This study presents an integrated engineering assessment of the Gerusernay embankment dam located in Adihforom Woreda, Tigray Region, northern Ethiopia, a water-scarce area characterized by high rainfall variability and recurrent drought. The assessment focuses on hydrological adequacy, seepage behavior, engineering geological conditions, and construction performance to evaluate the dam’s functionality and safety under site-specific conditions. The methodology combines field observations, water balance analysis, and seepage evaluation to examine system performance in an ungauged catchment context.The results indicate that overall seepage remains within acceptable design limits; however, localized seepage losses associated with unfavorable geological conditions and construction deficiencies were identified. Hydrological analysis reveals that limited and variable inflow significantly constrains reservoir performance, highlighting the critical role of catchment diversion in augmenting water availability and reducing hydrological uncertainty. In addition, gaps in construction quality, including incomplete implementation of design provisions and inadequate material control, were found to adversely affect system efficiency and reliability.The findings underscore the importance of integrated hydrological and geotechnical assessment, improved site investigation, and strict construction supervision to ensure the long-term performance of embankment dams in semi-arid environments. The study provides practical insights for enhancing the design, construction, and management of water storage infrastructure in Tigray and similar water-stressed regions.
